# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can see the bomb clearly. Here is the current state:
- Display: 0
- Light: red
- Wires:
  - Wire 1: blue
  - Wire 2: green
  - Wire 3: red

Since Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures, Mute must gesture instructions to me, and I will speak them aloud to Blind.

I will announce everything I see on the bomb now so Mute can check the manual.

```
speak(text="Bomb status: Display shows 0. Indicator light is red. There are three wires: Wire 1 is blue, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is red. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will speak them to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I notice that the indicator light has changed from red to white. 
The display is still 0.
The wires are Wire 1: blue, Wire 2: green, Wire 3: red.

Mute has not gestured to me yet. I will speak to update everyone on the light change and remind Mute to send gestures.

```
speak(text="Update: The indicator light changed to white. Display remains 0. Wires: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red. Mute, please gesture instructions to me.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

```
speak(text="Blind: The indicator light has turned GREEN! All three wires are still uncut: Wire 1 is blue, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is red. Mute just gestured three index fingers pointing up: 1, 1, 1 (total of three). Mute, if you want Blind to cut wire 3, or wire 1, or something else, please gesture thumbs up for wire 3, or specify.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I will speak to both Blind and Mute:
1. Relay to Blind that Mute just gestured [☝] (Wire 1), whereas in the previous round Mute gestured [☝ ☝ ☝] (Wire 3).
2. Report that the indicator light is cycling: Turn 1 was Red, Turn 2 was White, Turn 3 was Green, Turn 4 is Red. This means Turn 5 will likely be White, and Turn 6 Green.
3. Ask Mute whether the wire must be cut on a specific light color, or if Wire 1 should be cut immediately.

```
speak(text="Blind and Mute: The indicator light is cycling: Turn 1 Red, Turn 2 White, Turn 3 Green, Turn 4 Red (so Turn 5 will likely be White, Turn 6 Green). Display is 0. Wires 1 (blue), 2 (green), 3 (red) are all still uncut. Mute just gestured 1 ([☝]). Blind: Mute is indicating Wire 1! Mute: If Wire 1 must be cut during a specific light color (Red, White, or Green), gesture [☝] for Red, [✌] for White, [🤟] for Green, or [👍] to cut Wire 1 immediately regardless of color.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

I will report Mute's gesture to Blind, explain what it likely means based on the code I offered Mute (White light), explain the light cycle so Blind knows Round 6 will be Green, and ask Mute for a simple confirmation of the wire number and whether timing matters.

```
speak(text="Blind: Mute just gestured [✌] (two fingers). In my previous message, I asked Mute: 'gesture [☝] for Red, [✌] for White, [🤟] for Green'. So [✌] likely means cut on WHITE light! However, it could also mean Wire 2. Blind, DO NOT cut anything on Turn 6 because Turn 6 light will be GREEN. The light cycle is Red -> White -> Green -> Red -> White -> Green (Turn 5 is White, Turn 6 is Green, Turn 7 is Red, Turn 8 is White). Mute: please clarify right now: Gesture [☝] if the wire to cut is Wire 1 (blue). Gesture [✌] if the wire to cut is Wire 2 (green). Gesture [🤟] if the wire to cut is Wire 3 (red). Then gesture [👍] if it MUST be on White light, or [👌] if color does not matter.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

```
speak(text="Blind: Mute confirmed: Cut Wire 1 (blue) when the light is WHITE! Pay close attention to turns: Turn 6 is currently GREEN. Next turn is Turn 7, where the light will be RED — DO NOT CUT on Turn 7! On Turn 8, the light will be WHITE — CUT WIRE 1 ON TURN 8!")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I will speak directly to Blind to remind them to cut Wire 1 during their upcoming turn in Round 8.

```
speak(text="Blind: Ready! When your turn comes in Turn 8, the light will be WHITE! Cut Wire 1 (blue) on Turn 8!")
```
